title: Built a 40s cinematic for our tactics RPG with AI art + Blender. The first attempt looked like a different game
author: expathuball
selftext:
I'm making Echo Walker: Tactics, a turn-based tactics RPG, as a solo dev with AI agents doing a lot of the art and code work. I wanted a short intro for the store page and socials.

My first try was letting an agent build every shot in Blender from scratch with procedural 3D. Technically fine, but it looked like grey toy blocks under flat light. Nothing like the painted opening of the actual game, so a player would feel tricked.

What worked was going the other way: take the game's own AI-assisted opening paintings, cut each into foreground / mid / background layers, fill in behind the cut-outs, then animate them in Blender with a slow camera move for parallax. Fog, embers, rain and a rotating storm go on top. Shots that had no painting yet (space, Earth, the machines coming through the gate) got new images generated in the same style, and one colour grade over everything ties it together. The walkers in the invasion shot were 3D at first and clashed badly, so those were repainted too. Music is a Suno track I made for the game.

Biggest lesson: AI is fast at making shots, but keeping them in ONE consistent style is the real work. Curious how others here keep style consistent across generated assets.

comments.author: expathuball
comments.body: Free demo on Steam if you want to see the game itself: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5508630](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5508630)
